verifications.claim: The Artemis II mission is scheduled to launch on April 1, 2026.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: 'Launch date April 1, 2026, 22:35:12 UTC'; R2: 'NASA’s Artemis II mission is set to launch on April 1, 2026'; R3: 'Artemis II lifted off at 6:35 p.m. EDT [April 1]'; similar in others.
verifications.reasoning: Multiple sources directly confirm the launch date as April 1, 2026.

verifications.claim: The Artemis II mission is scheduled to launch at 6:35 p.m. EDT.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: 'April 1, 2026, 22:35:12 UTC (6:35:12 p.m. EDT)'; R3: 'Artemis II lifted off at 6:35 p.m. EDT'; R5: 'Liftoff! ... at 6:35 p.m. ET'; R6: 'at 6:35 p.m. Eastern time.'

verifications.claim: The Artemis II mission has a launch window from 5:24–7:24 pm CT.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R2: 'The launch is scheduled for 5:24 pm CT, and the window is 5:24–7:24 pm CT.'

verifications.claim: The Artemis II mission is scheduled to launch from Kennedy Space Center, FL.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: 'Launch site Kennedy, LC-39B'; R2: 'at NASA’s Kennedy Space Center in Florida'; R3: 'from the Kennedy Space Center in Florida.'

verifications.claim: The Artemis II mission is a 10-day mission.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: 'approximately ten-day trip'; R3: '10-day Moon Mission'; R4: 'approximately 10-day test flight'; R5: 'over the next 10 days'; R7: '10-day mission'.
verifications.reasoning: Routinely described as 10-day mission, though precise duration is 9 days 1 hour.

verifications.claim: The Artemis II mission will take four astronauts.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: 'Crew size 4'; R2: 'Four astronauts'; R3: 'four astronauts'; etc.

verifications.claim: The Artemis II mission is a crewed flyby around the Moon.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: 'Crewed lunar flyby mission'; R2: 'crewed lunar flyby'; R3: 'mission around the moon'; etc.
verifications.reasoning: Explicitly described as crewed lunar flyby.

verifications.claim: The Artemis II mission marks the first human return to deep space since 1972.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: 'first crewed flight beyond low Earth orbit since Apollo 17 in 1972'; R3: 'first piloted moonshot since the end of the Apollo program 53 years ago'; R6: 'first time since Apollo 17.'

verifications.claim: The Artemis II mission liftoff is on the SLS rocket.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: 'Rocket Space Launch System'; R2: 'Space Launch System (SLS) rocket'; etc.

verifications.claim: The Artemis II mission's Initial Orbit is April 1–2.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: 'High Earth orbit and systems checkout ... Launch April 1 ... On flight day 2 [April 2] ...'; 'Earth orbiter Orbital departure April 2'.
verifications.reasoning: R1 details initial high Earth orbit on launch day (April 1) extending to TLI on April 2.

verifications.claim: During the Artemis II mission's Initial Orbit, the crew tests Orion capsule systems in high Earth orbit.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: 'High Earth orbit and systems checkout ... crew conducted system checkouts'; R4: 'thorough checkout of Orion’s systems while still relatively close to home'.
verifications.reasoning: Direct description of testing in high Earth orbit.

verifications.claim: The Artemis II mission's Translunar Injection is April 2.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: 'Orbital departure April 2, 2026'; 'On flight day 2 ... Orion performed a 5-minute, 49-second TLI burn'.

verifications.claim: During the Artemis II mission's Translunar Injection, there is an engine firing to leave Earth orbit for the Moon.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: 'trans-lunar injection (TLI) burn to depart Earth orbit'; R4: 'translunar injection burn ... set Orion on the path to the Moon'.

verifications.claim: The Artemis II mission's Lunar Flyby is April 6.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: 'Closest approach April 6, 2026, 23:00 UTC'; 'On flight day 6, Orion ... lunar flyby'.

verifications.claim: The Artemis II mission's Lunar Flyby is the closest approach to the Moon on Day 6.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: 'Flyby of Moon Closest approach April 6, 2026 ... On flight day 6 ... closest approach'.

verifications.claim: The Artemis II mission's Return & Splashdown is April 10.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: 'Landing date April 11, 2026, 00:07:27 UTC (April 10, 5:07:27 p.m. PDT)'; R8: 'Splashdown April 10'.

verifications.claim: During the Artemis II mission's Return & Splashdown, there is re-entry and landing in the Pacific Ocean.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: 'Splashdown occurred April 11, 2026 ... in the Pacific Ocean southwest of San Diego'; 'Re-entry and splashdown'.

verifications.claim: Backup launch dates for the Artemis II mission are available on April 2-6 and April 30.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: 'seven two-hour launch windows were announced for 1–6 and April 30'; R2: 'April 2: 6:22 pm CDT ... April 3: 7:00 pm CDT ... April 4: 7:53 pm CDT ... April 5: 8:40 pm CDT ... April 6: 9:36 pm CDT April 30: 5:06 pm CDT'.
